title: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones - Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1 - Preventive vs Corrective Maintenance
exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: According to mobile phone maintenance guidelines, which of the following activities is best described as preventive maintenance?
options: Cleaning the charging port and internal components
Replacing a burnt-out resistor on the motherboard
questions.explain: Cleaning is a routine action taken to prevent future hardware failures, making it a classic example of preventive maintenance, whereas replacing broken parts is classified as corrective maintenance.
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: If a mobile phone is diagnosed with a physically damaged microphone, the act of desoldering the old part and soldering a new one is an example of:
questions.explain: Corrective maintenance involves fixing or replacing components that have already failed or broken, such as removing a damaged microphone and installing a functional one to restore operation.
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: During an audit of a repair workshop's workflow, a technician classifies regular board cleaning and removing dust buildup. This process ultimately minimizes the need for which subsequent procedure?
questions.explain: By performing regular preventive maintenance like removing dust and debris, a technician reduces the likelihood of component failure, thus minimizing the need for reactive, corrective maintenance later.
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which pair directly represents the concepts of 'Preventive' and 'Corrective' maintenance respectively, as strictly defined by the guidelines?
options: Replacing damaged parts vs. Using a heat gun
questions.explain: Preventive maintenance includes proactive actions like cleaning to avoid future issues, while corrective maintenance involves reactive actions like replacing components that are already broken.
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: Which component is most accurately described as a 'damaged part' that would require replacing under Corrective Maintenance?
questions.explain: Corrective maintenance responds to existing physical faults. A shattered glass digitizer is a broken hardware piece that must be entirely replaced to restore function, making it a clear corrective task.
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: A phone dropped in water requires thorough cleaning of the motherboard to prevent future corrosion, but also needs its shorted backlight filter replaced. How is this combined workflow classified according to the GSM guidelines?
questions.explain: Cleaning the board clears away minerals that cause future corrosion (preventive maintenance), while replacing the shorted backlight filter addresses an already broken component (corrective maintenance).
questions.exam: WASSCE Maintenance and Repair of Mobile Phones
questions.subject: Computer Hardware and GSM Repairs 1

questions.q: A client brings in a phone with a completely dead logic board that requires a new main IC soldered on, software flashed via dongle, and external casing cleaned. Which phase of this service definitively matches 'preventive maintenance' as per the source text?
questions.explain: Cleaning the external casing prevents future accumulation of dirt and grime in ports and buttons, acting as a preventive measure. In contrast, soldering ICs and flashing software fix existing issues, which is corrective maintenance.
